It's better to redirect because then both the output for `By` and klog log output show up in a single block, with correct ordering.

Here's a patch for klog redirection:
```diff
diff --git a/test/e2e/framework/test_context.go b/test/e2e/framework/test_context.go
index 77f28b03e3a..1704d0c07d7 100644
--- a/test/e2e/framework/test_context.go
+++ b/test/e2e/framework/test_context.go
@@ -28,6 +28,8 @@ import (
        "strings"
        "time"
 
+       "github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2"
+
        restclient "k8s.io/client-go/rest"
        "k8s.io/client-go/tools/clientcmd"
        clientcmdapi "k8s.io/client-go/tools/clientcmd/api"
@@ -434,8 +436,21 @@ func GenerateSecureToken(tokenLen int) (string, error) {
 }
 
 // AfterReadingAllFlags makes changes to the context after all flags
-// have been read.
+// have been read and prepares the process for a test run.
 func AfterReadingAllFlags(t *TestContextType) {
+       // Reconfigure klog so that output goes to the GinkgoWriter instead
+       // of stderr. The advantage is that it then gets interleaved properly
+       // with output that goes to GinkgoWriter (By, Logf).
+       //
+       // These flags are not exposed via the normal command line flag set,
+       // therefore we have to use our own private one here.
+       var fs flag.FlagSet
+       klog.InitFlags(&fs)
+       fs.Set("logtostderr", "false")
+       fs.Set("alsologtostderr", "false")
+       fs.Set("one_output", "true")
+       klog.SetOutput(ginkgo.GinkgoWriter)
+
        // Only set a default host if one won't be supplied via kubeconfig
        if len(t.Host) == 0 && len(t.KubeConfig) == 0 {
                // Check if we can use the in-cluster config
```

I think we should:
- support a new target that is ginkgo version independent
- temporarily support the old vendor path and throw a warning to migrate

The test-infra + kind PRs won't cover all of CI just off the top of my head and I'm sure there's more of these out there.

I agree that a generic `make all WHAT=ginkgo` is useful.

I am less sure about supporting `make all WHAT=vendor/github.com/onsi/ginkgo/ginkgo`. This will let CIs build the ginkgo binary, but if they then invoke it without `-junit-report` or `-timeout=24h`, then it won't work as expected (no report, times out after 1 hour).

This leads me to one idea: what if we support `make all WHAT=vendor/github.com/onsi/ginkgo/ginkgo`, but then put a script there which wraps the actual binary and invokes it as `ginkgo-v2 -timeout 24h "$@"`? Even better, if it finds a `-report-dir` and `-report-prefix` parameter, it could inject `-junit-report=<report-file>`, too.

With that in place, we might not have to change any CI at all.

If we do that, what should `WHAT=ginkgo` produce? It's unclear, so perhaps we shouldn't support it after all.

Implementing my wrapper script idea turned out to be harder. I currently have this hack (?!):
```
diff --git a/hack/lib/golang.sh b/hack/lib/golang.sh
index 68f77e408e1..536837f7e93 100755
--- a/hack/lib/golang.sh
+++ b/hack/lib/golang.sh
@@ -571,6 +571,27 @@ kube::golang::place_bins() {
         rsync -pc {} "${KUBE_OUTPUT_BINPATH}/${platform}" \;
     fi
   done
+
+  # ginkgo v2 must be called with a -timeout=24h parameter to get
+  # the same behavior as in ginkgo v1. We achieve that via a wrapper
+  # script.
+  set -x
+  for ginkgo in "${KUBE_OUTPUT_BINPATH}/${host_platform}/ginkgo" "${KUBE_GOPATH}"/bin/ginkgo; do
+    if [ -x "${ginkgo}" ] && ! grep -q "ginkgo wrapper script" "${ginkgo}"; then
+       V=2 kube::log::status "Wrapping $ginkgo"
+       mv "${ginkgo}" "${ginkgo}".bin
+       cat >"${ginkgo}" <<EOF
+#!/bin/sh
+#
+# This is a ginkgo wrapper script. It ensures that the actual ginkgo
+# binary uses the same defaults as gingko v1.
+
+exec "${ginkgo}.bin" --timeout=24h "\$@"
+EOF
+      chmod a+rx "${ginkgo}"
+    fi
+  done
+  set +x
 }
```

This fails in two ways:
```
go install github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2/ginkgo: build output "/nvme/gopath/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/_output/local/go/bin/ginkgo" already exists and is not an object file
```

That's after it has been built and wrapped before. Could be fixed by deleting the file first?

But the wrapper script also needs to be more complicated. The "--timeout" parameter is only accepted after the "run" command, so the script would have to inspect parameters instead of simply prepending it as it is done now.

Is that worth further work?

We discussed the `WHAT=ginkgo` topic a bit at KubeCon. There was no clear consensus, but overall I think the preference is to not have such a special target. The key argument against it for me is that it doesn't help when there are command line changes. I also retract my wrapper script - it's just too hacky.

JUnit via -report-dir will continue to work, so the breaking change is only the need to pass --timeout=24h and how to build. I suggest this as release note:
```

ACTION REQUIRED: When running test/e2e via the Ginkgo CLI, the v2 CLI must be used and `-timeout=24h` (or some other, suitable value) must be passed because the default timeout was reduced from 24h to 1h. issue_context.title: Updating the test framework to ginkgo 2.0
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Updating the test framework to ginkgo 2.0 will eventually happen I'm sure and I just wanted to have some notes related to this that people can reference.

### Why is this needed?

Just tracking issues that would be related to any updating of ginkgo from 1.0 to 2.0.
- [ ] Custom reporters deprecated https://onsi.github.io/ginkgo/MIGRATING_TO_V2#removed-custom-reporters
  - [ ] The junit reporter will easily be ported (they have a flag for that)
  - [ ] The progress reporter which makes real-time updates easier will take a little more work but should be fine. I'm happy to take this work when it is needed.

The code is okay, but the commit message says "Migrate to GinkgoWriter" which doesn't match the code. Perhaps just say "Adapt to new type of GinkgoWriter"?
Looks good now.

Rather than copying behavior out of the progressreporter into various Before/After hooks, why not keep them in functions attached to the reporter and call them from the hooks? - That way we keep the string-y parts together and keep things easier to understand in the future.

I agree call as a function within `ReportAfterEach` should be cleaner in case there are other similar things need to be managed in the `ReportAfterEach`. But the change in the `SynchronizedBeforeSuite`, `SynchronizedAfterSuite` are still necessary and it is trivial, we can keep it as is. WDYT?

The `SynchronizedBeforeSuite` / `SynchronizedAfterSuite` changes should definitely be function calls into here - they set arbitrary strings on state that is then used by external tools, keeping them in one place is super useful.
